title: Symphony Step Runner: idempotent upgrade choreography and guardrails for Private deployments
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers require deterministic, auditable, and reversible upgrades that can safely run schema+service migrations across mixed-version clusters with strict uptime requirements. Current ad-hoc scripts and one-off playbooks produce inconsistent outcomes and high manual coordination costs for large customers.

Goal: Deliver a composable upgrade orchestration component — Symphony Step Runner — that executes a configurable sequence of idempotent steps (preflight, schema migration, service rollout, postcheck), exposes programmable rollback/abort, integrates with LTS channels and rollout gates, and records an auditable execution trace for compliance and debugging.

Scope: MVP implements: preflight checks (node health, version compatibility, storage snapshots), step definitions (shell/Helm/K8s job/SQL), idempotency tokens, transactional step boundaries, canary step execution, global rollout gates (time-window, manual-approval, metric thresholds), pause/resume APIs, rollback hooks, and telemetry events sent to the console for per-upgrade traces.

Out of scope for MVP: full multi-cluster parallel coordinator and automated cross-region traffic shifting (future work).

Acceptance criteria: 
- A documented upgrade plan can be created and executed via CLI and Private Console with a single command.
- Each step records start/stop status, stdout/stderr, and produces deterministic outcome codes and stable idempotency keys.
- Canary steps can be configured at step granularity; system supports automatic rollback when configured SLO/metric thresholds are breached.
- Upgrades can be paused, resumed, and aborted; abort triggers configured rollback hooks.
- Audit log for each upgrade is stored in customer-managed object store and accessible via Console.
- End-to-end integration test harness validates a multi-step upgrade against a 3-node mixed-version cluster with simulated failure injection.

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Orchestration model: adopt a step-runner choreography pattern instead of a single monolithic orchestrator to minimize blast radius for on-prem control-plane constraints. Step Runner workers execute on customer clusters; a lightweight conductor in the control plane stores plan metadata and supervises progress. This balances privacy with operational control.
- Idempotency: each step must accept an idempotency token to make DB/schema steps and Helm upgrades re-runnable; we will provide wrappers for common operations and require contributors to implement idempotency for custom steps.
- Failure handling: prefer explicit compensating rollback hooks over automatic reverse-applies for destructive schema migrations; this reduces risk of data corruption but requires curated rollback steps in playbooks.
- Security: upgrade artifacts and logs must be encrypted in transit and at rest; Symphony will use customer KMS (via the existing KMS integration) for encryption keys.
- Observability: emit structured telemetry events compatible with Console traces and runtime-1.18 release tracing APIs.

Implementation milestones: 
1) Design review and API spec (PRD + OpenAPI) — 2 weeks.
2) Step Runner binary and plugin interface (K8s Job + local VM mode) — 3 weeks.
3) Preflight checks and snapshot hooks + idempotency wrappers — 2 weeks.
4) Canary gate integration + metrics evaluator service — 2 weeks.
5) Console integration for upgrade trace and manual approval UI — 3 weeks.
6) E2E test harness and customer staging runbook — 2 weeks.

Testing plan: 
- Unit tests for idempotency wrappers and step-state machine.
- Integration test harness that spins up a reproducible 3-node cluster (helm chart) with mixed versions, runs a sample upgrade plan that includes DB migration and node draining, injects failures, and asserts expected rollback/continue behavior.
- Internal dogfood: run against internal private cluster fleet and one selected customer staging environment.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: destructive schema migrations might not have reliable rollbacks. Mitigation: require snapshot+backup preflight step; enforce review of rollback hooks as part of release gating.
- Risk: long-running steps could exceed control-plane timeouts. Mitigation: implement heartbeat and checkpointing to allow resume across restart.
- Risk: customers with strict air-gapped setups may block telemetry. Mitigation: support white-label storage endpoints for audit logs and allow telemetry to be disabled with local log retention.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIVATE/Symphony+Step+Runner+Design,
openapi spec: https://git.redwood.ai/private-upgrades/symphony-api/spec.yaml,
example playbook: https://git.redwood.ai/private-upgrades/playbooks/mysql-safe-rollout.yaml

Next steps: schedule design review with Security and Customer Ops, finalize API, begin implementation of the K8s job executor and idempotency wrappers.
